payload.title: Talentichthys

{{Short description|Genus of extinct lungfish}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range =
[[Upper Devonian]], {{fossilrange|Famennian|Famennian|[[Famennian]]}} | image = Talentichthys kuragh (holotype, HRCT).jpg | image_caption = Details of the holotype based on [[HRCT]] data | display_parents = 2 | genus = Talentichthys | parent_authority = Young & Lu, [[2026 in paleoichthyology|2026]] | species = kuragh | authority = Young & Lu, 2026 }} '''''Talentichthys''''' ({{lit|[[John Alfred Talent|Talent]] fish}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[lungfish]] ([[Class (biology)|class]] Dipnoi) in the family [[Holodontidae]] known from the [[Upper Devonian]] ([[Famennian]] age) [[Shogrãm Formation]] of Pakistan. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Talentichthys kuragh''''', known from a partial skull. == Discovery and naming == [[File:Talentichthys kuragh (holotype, ANU V3736).jpg|thumb|left|Holotype as preserved]] The ''Talentichthys'' fossil material was discovered in 1976 by a team including [[John Alfred Talent|John A. Talent]] and others while they were measuring the [[stratigraphic]] section at Kurãgh Spur, about {{convert|55|km|mi}} northeast of [[Chitral]], Pakistan. These outcrops are assigned to the [[Shogrãm Formation]]. Curiously, a publication ten years prior by V. H. Gupta and Robert H. Denison had noted the seemingly significant discovery of a partial fossil skull and scales of a lungfish from nearby, in [[Kashmir]], India, a claim noted to be surprising, given its remote locality and the few fossils known from that area. However, later investigations showed that the descriptions of many Himalayan specimens that Gupta was involved with were fraudulent; this alleged lungfish fossil was actually from the Achanarras Quarry of Scotland. The Pakistani fossil went largely unnoticed in the years following its discovery, being acknowledged only vaguely as a dipnoan occurrence labeled on a figure by Talent et al. in 1999. In 2009, Gavin C. Young found the specimen, embedded in a piece of [[limestone]], in an 'oddments drawer' of a collection of fossil fish at the [[Australian National University]] (ANU). This fossil, provisionally catalogued as ANU V3736, had been sent to the ANU for identification but was regarded as too fragmentary to provide much information. Later work will likely result in the specimen being re-[[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] at the [[Australian Museum]] or returned to an institution in Pakistan. In 2018, [[high-resolution computed tomography]] (HRCT) scans were made of the skull to study it in greater detail, including its internal anatomy, nerve canals, and other structures of the [[braincase]]. The skull is incomplete, preserving only the [[Anatomical terms of location#Anterior and posterior|anterior]] (toward the front) snout region. In 2026, Gavin C. Young and Jing Lu [[Species description|described]] ''Talentichthys kuragh'' as a new genus and species of holodontid lungfish based on these fossil remains, establishing ANU V3736 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Talentichthys'', honors John A. Talent, the discoverer of the only known specimen, combined with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|[[:wikt:ichthys|ichthys]]}}, meaning {{gloss|fish}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''kuragh'', references the stratigraphic section of the same name from which the holotype was collected. == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Young |first1=Gavin C. |last2=Lu |first2=Jing |date=October 2026 |title=A new Devonian lungfish from the western Karakoram of northern Pakistan |journal=[[Palaeoworld]] |language=en |volume=35 |issue=5 |article-number=201130 |doi=10.1016/j.palwor.2026.201130 |doi-access=free}} {{Cite journal |last1=Gupta |first1=V.
